content:
The image shows soybean seeds held in a hand. Key observations:

- **Affected part**: Seeds (harvested soybeans)
- **Visual features**: Mix of normal tan/yellow seeds and seeds with purple/violet discoloration covering portions of the seed coat
- **Pattern**: Purple staining is irregular, covering parts or all of the seed surface on affected seeds
- **No fungal growth visible** on the surface; the discoloration is within the seed coat itself

This is a classic presentation of **Purple Seed Stain**, caused by *Cercospora kikuchii*. The hallmark symptom is exactly this: purple to violet discoloration of the soybean seed coat, ranging from small spots to complete coverage. The mix of healthy (tan) and stained (purple) seeds in the same handful is characteristic.

This is distinct from general Cercospora leaf blight (which affects leaves) — the seed stain form specifically presents as this purple seed coat discoloration.
